verdict: No treatment passes retention unchanged. Prefer the dramatist's ordering of draft refinement followed by the separate DORA examination, with an honest promise of two professional actions. Its claimed delayed revelation and several pen states must be rewritten before lock.

parent_challenges_answered.delayed_ready_suffix: Agreed. READY FOR REVIEW at 94 seconds merely spells out what the first human review already demonstrates. A delayed text reveal is not a new fact or an Act 3 test.
parent_challenges_answered.pen_employed: Reject The Pen Is Still Employed. Employment is an unsupported outcome and the phrase invites a jobs-preservation inference.
parent_challenges_answered.pose_only_states: Agreed. Riding a rail, bridging outputs, facing a report and being held elsewhere are mostly placement changes. A repeatable silhouette is continuity, not transformation.
parent_challenges_answered.honest_primary_promise: Replace what-secretly-remains with an explicit early promise: follow two useful outputs into two different professional actions. Paying the promise means completing the illustrated pair around 90 seconds, not hiding that people review work.
parent_challenges_answered.test_scope: Act 3 can compare the accomplished preparation with the next documented professional work. It cannot prove net productivity, actual error rates, compliance or human time saved.
parent_challenges_answered.narration_and_credits: Narration must occupy 112–130 seconds, targeting 120, with 200–220 future VO words. Append 12.3 seconds of credits afterward. A 120-second narration yields 132.3 seconds total.

Distinct mailroom, records aisle, drafting bay and review table are plausible real sets.
The two mechanisms are separate before 59 seconds, with no timing statistic conflation.
The table at 59–69 seconds gives the machines credit for substantial preparation.
problems: The pen's professional purpose is apparent at the 69-second review scene. Keeping it parked until 90 does not preserve the primary question.

The secondary question asks whether FIRST DRAFT will disappear merely because the page looks neat. Its continued presence at 103 seconds supplies no new fact or action. It is required status continuity.
The 93–105-second section shuffle and persistent tag risk twelve seconds of padding after the actual edit has already landed.
Most five pen states are positions. One late edit cannot retroactively make riding and bridging into transformations.
The title makes an unsupported employment implication.
peer_challenges.sag_at_80: Moderate. The unused pen seems artificially withheld while report review already occurs. Let a visible professional action proceed instead of saving the obvious hand pickup.
peer_challenges.act3: The report examination and draft refinement are substantive; the tag-survival reveal is a restatement.
peer_challenges.source_honesty: Generally careful. Keep first-draft status continuously legible; do not imply a real document remains unapproved after an actual completed approval. Show no actual approval outcome.
peer_challenges.three_real_sets: Pass in treatment if the named rooms have distinct physical layouts; the company foyer alone cannot substitute for a full third work set.
peer_challenges.recommended_graft: Keep one economical desk-physics gag and the successful-output beat. Drop the employed title and the 103-second label payoff.

No new hero drawing is necessary.

peer_challenges.sag_at_80: The refinement can hold attention at 78. Sag begins immediately after it if the next twelve seconds only install a phrase already understood.
peer_challenges.act3: Keep the source-described actions. Cut the claim that the larger desk legend creates an earned reveal.

Report examination followed by generated-section refinement gives Act 3 actual work.

The primary answer is demonstrated as soon as professional work begins at 73 seconds. The secondary edit at 85 completes the same conceptual answer.
The 95–106-second depth separation and 114–120-second inscription repeat the boundary twice after the actions have established it.

The submitted future VO is beyond the no-VO request for this phase and should not be treated as locked copy.
peer_challenges.sag_at_80: Lowest risk while the report-to-draft action changes at 84, but the 95–120 tail becomes three versions of the same conclusion.
peer_challenges.act3: Strong base. Shorten the output-gallery contemplation to one clear success beat, then let the two professional actions provide the duration.

peer_challenges.three_real_sets: Pass with consolidation. Handoff bench, output gallery and review/editing desk are not automatically four separate sets; use at least three genuinely different rooms or spatial layouts.
peer_challenges.recommended_graft: Keep appreciative stance and housings-recede reset. Replace the late spatial slogan with completion of the second promised action.

own_pitch_concessions: My primary question is also answered at the first human refinement at 69–79 seconds. Calling the DORA examination at 90 a revelation is overstated.
My pen parked over a cutaway and later turned toward a report are poses, not new physical states.
My first-scene reaching hand makes the secret pen-role premise even less credible.
My 91–102-second synthesis is too long if it only preserves both jobs in a wide frame.
My final scene incorrectly shares narration time with credits.
My best structural choice is the order: generated section visibly changes first, then a distinct record-review action completes the pair at about 90 seconds.

winner_plus_graft.winner: DRAMATIST, conditional on the revisions below
winner_plus_graft.reason: The two actual professional actions finish at 78 and 90 seconds, already giving the film a useful change of material and verb near 80. This is the least disruptive route to an honest late completion rather than an artificial late discovery.

grafts.keep: The clean API/prebuilt-logic versus separate LLM/Bedrock mechanism comparison, complete before 60 seconds.
A brief 61–67-second reset where housings recede and both useful outputs retain substance and scale.
One early pen/cap desk-physics gag. Keep humor in ordinary objects, not corporate identity or employment.

winner_plus_graft.title_direction: Two Jobs After Ready, or retain The Pen Still Has Work only if copy clearly refers to the pen's depicted use and avoids employment claims.

primary_loop_revision.promise: Two prepared outputs. Follow what the professional does with each.
primary_loop_revision.progress: One action is visibly completed around 77 seconds; the second is explicitly still to be shown, not an undisclosed caveat.
primary_loop_revision.payoff: The second illustrated professional action completes the promised pair: generated sections are refined; the separate report is examined for a determination.
primary_loop_revision.distinction: This is a demonstration promise, not a mystery about whether humans exist or proof that a final determination was made.

secondary_loop_revision.promise: A small physical cap puzzle: the removed cap catches briefly on the pen's spring clip as the separate draft appears. The pen and cap will have to fit together to write.
secondary_loop_revision.payoff: The clip releases and the cap seats on the pen's rear; the nib contacts the draft and leaves a neutral editorial mark as a section is refined.
secondary_loop_revision.honesty: This is openly cartoon prop mechanics in an illustrative office, not a claim about a KGS product defect, a stuck workflow or elapsed waiting time. It is distinct from the primary factual promise.
secondary_loop_revision.caution: Use one brief plant and one brief release. Do not hold a motion for twenty-eight seconds or make cap trouble delay the professional.

physical_pen_states.state: Closed: cap encloses the nib; spring clip lies flush against the cap.
Clipped: the spring clip flexes around a thin generic record-divider lip, visibly changing its gap; cap still encloses nib.
Opened: cap separates, exposing the nib; cap edge momentarily catches the spring clip, planting the physical loop.
Working assembly: clip releases, cap posts onto the rear, making the pen visibly longer; nib contacts the draft and lays one neutral annotation stroke.

Used and open: the same posted cap and exposed nib remain, with the prior stroke visible in the adjacent refined draft; the hand uses the pen as a pointer while examining the separate report. This last use is functional continuity, not counted as a fifth material transformation.

winner_plus_graft.object_state_count: Four defensible physical configurations, followed by a fifth functional use. Do not advertise five transformations. The four-state minimum is met through cap enclosure, clip flex, cap separation and posted-cap writing configuration.

beats: 61–67: both machine preparation tasks visibly succeed; no failure, timer or empty output.
67–78: generated section is selected and neutrally refined; no false factual defect, final status or signature.
78–90: cut to the separate DORA report; professional opens and examines it for a determination, with no invented specific vendor verdict.
90–93: one compact comparison preserves both accomplishments. This is the pair's completion, not another revelation.
act3_revision.source_scope: AWS-described process only. Human examination and refinement are illustrated; the exact paper gesture is explanatory staging.
act3_revision.no_sag_rule: At about 78 seconds change material, professional verb and camera scale. Do not reserve an obvious pen pickup or label suffix for a false climax.

winner_plus_graft.tail_revision: Use the remaining narration for the specific current-announcement/earlier-example distinction and the named KGS–Koniag Alaska connection, expressed once. State the announcement's unquantified Alaska return briefly if retained. Button within the full 112–130-second narration; then 12.3 seconds of credits.
winner_plus_graft.padding_test: A shorter cut must still show the report and the generated section receiving different professional actions. The essential late material is those two actions. A twelve-second READY placement, prolonged paired-output hold, or repeated final phrase does not earn extra duration.

lock_conditions: Lock a fresh treatment with run_date 2026-09-13, 200–220 words planned, and 112–130 seconds of narration plus 12.3 seconds of credits.
Do not conceal API/rules versus LLM distinction; establish both before 60 seconds.
Use at least three physically distinct sets and four scales, not relabeled copies of one tabletop.
Replace all claims of surprise at human review with the openly promised pair of actions.
Make actual cap/clip/nib geometry changes visible at phone scale; no approval stamp, signed contract or invented error.
No stopwatch, portfolio arithmetic, employment implication, local financial-return inference or cultural characterization.
